newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sees early signs of El Nino in Pacific.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sees early signs of El Nino in Pacific.

text.p: Conditions in the tropical Pacific indicate a destructive weather system known as El Nino may be forming, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration said Thursday.

"The evolution of the atmospheric and oceanic conditions in the tropical Pacific during the past few months are early indications of warm episode, El Nino, conditions," the agency's climate prediction center said.
An El Nino occurs every two to seven years, and dumps heavy rainfall on the southern tier of the United States and Peru.
An El Nino can also cause destructive flooding and drought in northeast Brazil, southeastern Africa and the west Pacific, affecting crops and homes.

"The first half of the 1990s is unusual in that four out of five years featured warm episode conditions (El Ninos) in the tropical Pacific," the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration said in a statement. "However, a cold episode occurred in 1995/96 and its effects lingered until late 1996."
Government meterologists gather atmospheric and oceanic data from a network of buoys that measure temperature, currents and winds.
The weather phenomonon has been nicknamed "El Nino," the Spanish name for the Christ Child because it usually occurs late in the year near Christmas.
